goal_title: Book: Soft Bodies & Morphogenesis: Matter That Finds Its Shape — improvements from the spine reading
why: The whole spine was read as a book on 2026-09-24, one sequence at a time, and every stumble, false claim or broken handover in softbodies became a task Palle can pick up one at a time. Reader: the VR visitor.
success_criteria: every open task here is done or skipped with a note
the chapters read through without a stumble in the headset
every code excerpt and number in the chapters matches the source

book.title: Soft Bodies & Morphogenesis: Matter That Finds Its Shape

reading.arc: The sequence takes a body from a single yielding cube to a surface cut out of a field. It opens by asking what holds a deformable thing together (three coefficients on a desk, a mill that can be halted while the sphere goes on moving), then which points are forbidden to move (pins against a support that turns out to be scenery), then what changes when the support itself is driven (the carousel), when the architecture is the body (breathing walls), how to compare contacts honestly (a gallery with replay, hold and variation), and what a frozen form keeps of the process that made it (an instrument that feeds back on its own reading, a vessel reconstructed at 40/200/400 steps). It then turns on resemblance itself: radiolaria that look alive without any simulation. Two field-to-form mappings close it, Gray-Scott chemistry and a gyroid whose master control is called entropy, and the last hall asks who connected the controls. The discipline throughout is that every control is described by what it does and what it does not do, so the reader learns to separate material, boundary, drive, contact, instrument and name.
holds: The desk: every hall carries the same soft_workshop_console with five or six named controls, a two-line readout and a RULE card; the prose addresses the controls in capitals, so the reader always knows what is at hand.

The refrain 'it does X; it does not do Y' (RESET restores coefficients, not vertices; STOP zeroes the rate, not velocity or gravity; HOLD DRIVE holds phase, not vertices; RELEASE restores pins, not an original body; FEEDBACK off restores pressure, not the body you had).

Carried objects: the four stopped spheres (softstopscene) stand in Cloth and return in Reaction as 'soft-body samples'; radiolaria is flagged in hall 1 as a warning to keep for later and delivered in hall 7; the entropy surface stands in Playground as 'field sculpture' before its own hall; the cloth strips carry from Cloth into Carousel.

The pin thread: pinned points named as part of the cube's conditions, then PINS eight-two-none, then a driven pin, then pinned wall edges, then HOLD pinning every vertex, then the vessel's pinned upper region.
The resemblance-versus-mechanism thread: 'Calling it breathing is an invitation to bodily recognition', radiolaria's 'recognition before explanation', the parameter 'called entropy in the source'.
Each chapter ends by naming the next hall's question, and each title is a question the hall answers with a control.

hall_notes.note: Opens with the cube yielding and the three coefficients (stiffness, damping, pressure; all three assignments verified in jelly_cube.gd:79/87/95), then the mill whose drive can be held while the sphere's physics continues. Reads cleanly and plants radiolaria as a warning for later; it reaches back to Transformation rather than receiving the previous sequence's closing question.

The strongest chapter and more than twice the length of the others: eight strips, a support that vanishes while the held edge stays, the pin rule shown in code (exactly soft_workshop.gd:95-97; 8 of 112 vertices per strip, PlaneMesh 6x12 subdivisions), PINS eight-to-two, RELEASE, REBUILD, then the four stopped spheres. One instruction order is wrong (LANDING removes the rail before the reader is told to watch the rail) and the last line promises the wrong hanging body for the next hall.

Driven hub in radians per second (revolving_joy_ride.gd:15, 293), SPEED/REVERSE/STOP each described by what they leave running; a short, clear chapter that correctly says the cloth beside it keeps a fixed support and lists the sticks, cubes, flex pad and mushroom that are actually on the map.

The sine-to-pressure bridge is exact (breathing_room_scene.gd:12-13) and the 'invitation to bodily recognition' paragraph is the sequence's ethical centre. It names three of the desk's five controls and closes with the builder phrase 'the museum crossing', which a visitor cannot parse.

Replay, variation, hold, release and group are all real and all rebuild (softbody_test_gallery.gd:665-689); the named cells belong to the visible group. Reads as a careful method chapter about not mistaking proximity for a controlled comparison; only the example name 'Jelly' is from a group the reader is not looking at.

The instrument that measures an axis-aligned box (rounded_softbody.gd:757-767) and then feeds back on it is the sequence's sharpest idea, and the vessel section is right about closed topology and collision. It tells the reader SQUEEZE changes a strength without ever saying how a hand squeezes.

Recognition before explanation; the claim that COLOUR rebuilds geometry under an unpinned seed is true (radiolaria.gd:1157-1167 regenerates; seed 0 leaves the RNG unseeded). Short, exact, and it names its own place in the arc as a contrast, not a soft body.

Gray-Scott update, double buffering, wrapped edges and clamping all match turing_pattern_generator.gd:439-461. It alludes to the 100 STEPS button without naming it and invokes Turing and Gray-Scott with no attribution in a corpus that footnotes such names.

The lerp lines are exact (entropy_morphogenesis_vr.gd:172-174) and the closing paragraph is the sequence's summary. The LEVEL control it advertises silently fails on its fourth press, and 'the player' is the one lapse from the sequence's 'your body' vocabulary.

stumbles: SoftBodies_Cloth_Physics: 'Watch one meet the rail' follows the instruction to press LANDING, and the first press replaces the rail with the pan.

SoftBodies_Cloth_Physics to SoftBodies_Carusell: 'this time the cloth will know', but the driven support in the next hall carries soft spheres; the cloth there keeps a fixed support, as the next chapter itself says.
SoftBodies_Obsticals: 'the museum crossing still has independent support' is builder vocabulary from the map's design notes, never defined for a visitor.
SoftBodies_Obsticals: the desk has STIFFNESS and RESET PHASE; the prose names only AMPLITUDE, RATE and HOLD DRIVE, so two buttons sit unexplained on the hall whose argument is 'drive versus solver'.
SoftBodies_Obsticals_Part2: 'A name like "Jelly"' points at a Part 1 cell while the opening group is Part 2.
SoftBodies_Playground_of_Joy: SQUEEZE is explained as a strength, but a headset visitor is never told that squeezing is holding the grip with a hand at the body.
Topology_Entropy_Morphogenesis: cycling LEVEL back to 'minimal' leaves the threshold where 'broken' put it; the readout shows the number not moving.
Topology_Entropy_Morphogenesis: 'too narrow for the player' is the only 'player' in the sequence; elsewhere it is 'your body' and 'the visitor'.
ProceduralGeneration_Reaction_Diffusion_Systems: 'A hundred updates' describes a button labelled 100 STEPS without naming it the way every other control is named.
SoftBodies_Soft_Body_Deformation: the opening does not receive the previous sequence's closing question ('What bodies are possible now?') and reaches back to Transformation instead.

keep.quote: Boundary conditions are not a detail of the setup. Here they are most of what you have been looking at.
A convincing support does not prove how a simulation is attached to it. You have just taken the support away and watched the attachment survive it.
Two questions leave this room together. What makes a body deform, and what makes us stop looking?
A soft appearance does not announce every freedom a body possesses.
A number that helped us look has become a number the body is asked to follow.
A frozen result lets us look longer. It also makes the timing of a decision disappear into the apparent permanence of a thing.
Desire can travel ahead of an explanation; a strange body can invite attention before we know how to describe it.
The point is not to exhaust desire by naming every rule. It is to gain enough purchase on a rule to change what it permits—and notice what the next construction still leaves out.

reading.handover_in: PG_Mirrored_Patterns closes: 'we have selected, guided, branched, connected, carved, sampled and copied... What bodies are possible now? We can answer with a construction, try its limits, and carry the unresolved part into the next hall.' SoftBodies_Soft_Body_Deformation opens with a cube that gives way, which does answer the question, but it never receives it: its only backward reference is 'We have already changed whole objects by translation, rotation and scale', two sequences back. The bodies thread is implicit; one sentence would make it explicit.
reading.handover_out: Strong and verified. Topology_Entropy_Morphogenesis ends on a summary of the sequence and 'notice what the next construction still leaves out'; ISO_Introduction opens 'A boundary made from values' and says outright 'The porous specimen in the previous room introduced the same distinction between values and visible form.' The entropy surface is a marching-cubes gyroid cut at a threshold (entropy_morphogenesis_vr.gd:197-209, LEVEL moves threshold_center), so ISO's LEVEL control continues exactly the question hall 9 opened.

tasks.title: LEVEL's return to 'minimal' does not move the threshold
tasks.spec:
[encounter] Topology_Entropy_Morphogenesis
Quote: “LEVEL changes the threshold arrangement.”
Why: The desk cycles minimal, thickened, pinched, broken; the fourth press sends 'minimal' but the artifact's level branch writes nothing for it, so threshold_center stays at 0.95 from 'broken', the surface regenerates unchanged and the readout shows the same threshold. The reader is told a control does something and watches it do nothing.
Do: In soft_workshop.gd's LEVEL branch, set model.threshold_center = 0.0 before applying 'minimal' (or make _apply_level write 0.0 for 'minimal' only when _built is true), so the cycle closes and the readout moves on every press.
Evidence: commons/artifacts/timing_machines/soft_workshop.gd:198 cycles ["minimal","thickened","pinched","broken"] through apply_grid_config; algorithms/spacetopology/entropy_morphogenesis/entropy_morphogenesis_vr.gd:150-159 _apply_level writes -0.60/0.60/0.95 for the other three and `_: pass` for minimal; :291-295 and :306-310 regenerate with the unchanged threshold_center; readout soft_workshop.gd:216 prints current_threshold.

tasks.title: Watch the rail before pressing LANDING
tasks.spec:
[prose] SoftBodies_Cloth_Physics
Quote: “LANDING exchanges the thing underneath them and drops them again. Watch one meet the rail: the contact is a line rather than a plane”
Why: The map opens this artifact on the rail, and the desk's first LANDING press installs the pan (two walls), so a reader who follows the sentence order watches the wrong contact. The line-versus-plane observation belongs to the opening state.

tasks.title: Say how a hand squeezes the body
tasks.spec:
[vr] SoftBodies_Playground_of_Joy
Quote: “SQUEEZE changes the strength used by the artifact's existing squeeze interaction.”
Why: In the headset the squeeze is holding the controller's grip with a hand within 0.25 m of the body, which pushes vertices away from the hand; the desk button only scales that push (and its third setting turns it off). A visitor who never grips sees SQUEEZE do nothing and cannot follow 'Watch the instrument as well as the silhouette'.

tasks.title: STIFFNESS is a fraction between nought and one, and the solver's effort is a pass count the panel does not show
tasks.spec:
Godot's SoftBody3D.linear_stiffness is bounded 0..1 ('higher values will result in a stiffer body, while lower values will increase the body's ability to bend'), the same 0..1 'stiffness' NOC's Matter.js constraints carry ('1 being fully rigid and 0 being completely soft', default 0.7): how much of each spring's error the solver corrects per pass, not a material modulus. jelly_cube.gd:193, cloth_straps.gd:360 and breathing_room.gd:85 all set simulation_precision = 5, the number of correction passes per physics tick, which no panel shows. Form Finding's Relaxation bench put exactly that knob on a panel (PASSES: nudged 1, worked 4, pressed 8, held 12) and showed a cloth stiffen with the count alone; the soft-body halls never say the engine's solver is the same kind of procedure.

Proposal: After the quoted sentences: 'STIFFNESS is a number between nought and one: how much of each spring's disagreement the solver corrects each time it looks. It is not a property of a material. It is an instruction to a procedure that looks five times a tick, and the bench in Form Finding showed you that the count alone can stiffen a cloth. A soft body in this engine is a set of distances being corrected, never solved.'[fn] Footnote: Godot SoftBody3D, linear_stiffness (0..1) and simulation_precision (default 5); the room did not write the solver.

tasks.title: What holds the cube together: the edges of its skin, and pressure where the inside should be
tasks.spec:
The SoftBody3D's springs are the edges of the subdivided BoxMesh (jelly_cube.gd:186-190): the surface only, nothing across the interior. NOC's soft-body character makes the lesson explicit: connections only around the perimeter 'would instantly collapse onto itself. This is where additional internal springs come into play.' Godot's answer is pressure instead of struts - pressure_coefficient, default 1.0 here - and the artifact's own header says what happens without it: 'at low pressure it drapes over the pedestal like cloth' (line 12). The hall's title question has this answer and the chapter does not give it.

Proposal: After the quoted sentences: 'What holds them is the skin. Every edge of the cube's surface is a spring asked to keep its length, and there is nothing across the inside. Take PRESSURE to nothing and the cube shows you: a bag of triangles with no interior drapes over its pedestal like cloth. Pressure is what this engine offers in place of the internal struts a soft body would otherwise need.' Verification: desktop lane, PRESSURE to 0, watch the drape.

tasks.title: Name the hinge, and the hub that nothing can push back
tasks.spec:
revolving_joy_ride.gd: the hub is a RigidBody3D with freeze = true in kinematic mode (99-103) and rotation.y += ride_speed * delta each physics step (291-293); each link hangs on a pair of PinJoint3D (140-153), NOC's revolute constraint ('a regular Constraint of length 0... the bodies can rotate around a common anchor point'). NOC's warning about assigned positions applies from the support's side: a kinematic hub is moved by assignment and pushed back by nothing, which is why the teardrops report the ride and the ride never reports the teardrops. The chapter has the fact ('prescribed') and neither the name of the joint nor the asymmetry.

Proposal: After the quoted sentences: 'The joints are hinges: pins of no length that let each link swing about a point on the one above it. The hub is different in kind. It is a body the solver may not push: its angle is written each step, and nothing the hanging bodies do reaches it. So the teardrops report the ride, and the ride never reports them.'

tasks.title: Say what ties the hundred and twelve points: across, down, and one diagonal
tasks.spec:
cloth_straps.gd:351-354 builds each strip as a PlaneMesh subdivided 6 across and 12 down (8 x 14 = 112 vertices), and a SoftBody3D's springs are the mesh's triangle edges: to the neighbour across, the neighbour below, and one neighbour on the diagonal of each cell. NOC's cloth exercise ties 'each particle with its vertical and horizontal neighbors' only; the diagonal is why a strip can swing without shearing into a parallelogram. The chapter counts the points and never says what ties them.
